correctness_confidence.basis: The manuscript transparently labels its core analytic inputs as unproved assumptions and correctly notes in Remark 3.6 and Appendix B that the naive O(g_k^2) bound is non-summable. However, even conditionally on those assumptions, the deductions in Sections 3, 5, and 6 contain material mathematical gaps, notably the undefined cross-scale map for observables in A_ell and an invalid application of infinite-time OS reconstruction and Laplace-transform clustering on a finite-time torus.

novelty.basis: The conceptual separation into a local bounded-observable layer and a fixed-physical-scale Creutz-ratio layer, together with the 2-loop window-compatibility arithmetic (Lemma 1.4), provides a clean organizational template. However, once the hard analytic inputs (Assumptions 3.5, 4.4, 4.7, 4.9, 5.5, A.2) are postulated, the remaining proofs reduce to elementary telescoping sums and standard textbook arguments.

reproducibility.basis: The mathematical deductions in the manuscript are concise and easily inspected statically, and Section 8 and Appendix C provide an explicit, honest concordance of all imported hypotheses and version changes. External Python verification scripts referenced in the text were not executed in this static review.

rigor.basis: While the logical accounting of assumptions is commendably explicit, the mathematical formulation lacks rigor in key places: Definition 2.4 does not specify how a lattice observable on link variables is embedded across changing lattice spacings a_k; Corollary 5.6 and Theorem 6.2 conflate periodic Euclidean time of length L with infinite Euclidean time [0, infinity); and Layer 2 postulates limits without connecting them to the Layer 1 state.

significance.basis: Because all major non-perturbative obstacles for 4D SU(N_c) Yang-Mills theory (summable RG-Cauchy convergence, uniform transfer-matrix spectral gap, uniform infrared Creutz-ratio positivity, and six lattice hypotheses) are assumed rather than proved, the manuscript functions as a conditional roadmap rather than a substantive advance toward solving the Millennium Problem.

potential_errors: In Lemma 6.1 and Lemma A.3, the uniform clustering rate m_0 along the lattice coordinate axes is asserted to hold unchanged for arbitrary Euclidean separation d via a chessboard estimate, whereas along a 4D lattice diagonal the coordinate separation is d/2, reducing the axis transfer-matrix decay rate by up to a factor of 2 unless full SO(4) rotational invariance is already established.

In Lemma A.3, the transfer matrix T_a acts on a single spatial slice Sigma_a, but observables O_1, O_2 in A_ell have physical diameter up to ell (spanning ell/a time slices); the spectral expansion of time-separated correlators does not address the multi-slice temporal support of O_1, O_2.

In Corollary 3.3, the unrenormalized field Phi_a(varphi) in Eq. (7) lacks vacuum subtraction and wave-function renormalization; as a -> 0 with g(a)^2 -> 0, (1/N_c) Re Tr U_p -> 1, so Phi_a(varphi) converges trivially to the deterministic constant integral of varphi.
strengths: Exemplary transparency regarding conditionality: Section 1.5, Section 8.1, Section 8.2, and Section 9 clearly document all unproved assumptions, imported hypotheses, and errata from earlier versions.

Honest identification of the summability obstruction in Remark 3.6 and Appendix B, demonstrating explicitly that the naive 2-loop asymptotic-freedom rate g_k^2 ~ c/k diverges logarithmically upon summation and thus cannot discharge Assumption 3.5.

Lemma 1.4 provides a clean, quantitative verification that for a fixed physical box size L, the dyadic lattice size L/a_k = 2^k L/a_0 grows slower than the exponential volume window exp(c_w/g_k^2) along the 2-loop trajectory.

Clear distinction in Appendix A (Remarks A.1 and A.6) between the spectral gap of Glauber/Langevin dynamics controlled by log-Sobolev inequalities and the Euclidean transfer-matrix spectral gap required for the physical mass gap.
strong_novelty_candidates: Lemma 1.4 (window-compatibility margin ratio c_w * 2 b_0 approx 4.5 comparing dyadic continuum scaling against the multiscale volume window along the 2-loop asymptotic-freedom trajectory).
summary: This manuscript (internally marked v3, AIRR v1) presents a conditional framework for constructing the continuum limit, Hilbert-space reconstruction, mass gap, and confinement of 4D SU(N_c) lattice Yang-Mills theory along dyadic lattice spacings a_k = a_0 2^{-k}. Following an audit of the companion series [E26I]-[E26IX], the paper explicitly treats both the underlying lattice functional inequalities and the core continuum-limit steps (summable RG-Cauchy bound in Assumption 3.5, infinite-volume Creutz-ratio existence and positivity in Assumptions 4.4/4.7/4.9, uniform transfer-matrix gap in Assumption A.2, and strong continuity in Assumption 5.5) as unproved hypotheses. While the manuscript's candor in cataloging these assumptions and proving the non-summability of the naive O(g_k^2) bound (Appendix B) is a major strength, the mathematical deductions from the stated assumptions remain elementary and suffer from several material flaws: (1) the cross-scale definition of observables in A_ell across different lattices Lambda_{a_k,L} is unspecified; (2) OS reconstruction and the infinite-time Laplace-transform mass-gap proof (Theorem 6.2) are performed on a four-torus with finite periodic Euclidean time L, where correlators wrap around at t = L and do not decay as t -> infinity; and (3) Layer 2 and the nontriviality claim (Theorem 7.1) are not logically bridged to the Layer 1 state.
unresolved_material_objections: Undefined cross-scale observable map in Layer 1: Definition 2.4 defines A_ell as functions of finitely many links on Lambda_{a,L}, whose link set changes with a. No embedding map identifying O in A_ell at spacing a with an observable at spacing a/2 is defined for Assumption 3.5 or Theorem 3.9. If O fixes a lattice-unit loop (e.g. a single plaquette), <O>_{a_k,L} -> 1 trivially as g_k -> 0; if O fixes a macroscopic loop of physical size <= ell by link subdivision, its unrenormalized expectation vanishes in 4D due to UV perimeter divergence.

Invalid infinite-time OS semigroup and Laplace-transform argument on a finite-time torus (Corollary 5.6, Theorem 6.2, Lemma A.3): By Remark 1.3 and Section 2.1, omega_L is the limit state on a four-torus of fixed physical period L in all 4 directions, including Euclidean time. On a torus of time period L, reflection positivity holds only on (0, L/2), time translation tau_t is L-periodic (so tau_t leaves (0, L/2) for t >= L/2), and two-point correlators in omega_L wrap around the temporal circle rather than decaying as e^{-m_0 t} for t -> infinity (Eq. 28).

Quantifier conflict between the finite volume window and infinite-volume limits: Lemma 1.4 verifies L/a_k <= exp(c_w/g_k^2) at fixed L as k -> infinity, but Assumption 4.4 takes L -> infinity at fixed a, and Lemma 6.1 states its bound for all L >= L_* and all a in (0, a_0] with a_0 independent of L. At any fixed a, taking L -> infinity exits the audited volume window L/a <= exp(c_w/g(a)^2 + O(1)).

Logical disconnection between Layer 1 and Layer 2 in Theorem 7.1 (Nontriviality): Layer 2 postulates the existence and positivity of infinite-volume Creutz-ratio limits directly (Assumptions 4.4, 4.7, 4.9) without proving that they represent expectations in the Layer 1 state omega_L (or lim_{L->infinity} omega_L). Thus, sigma_phys > 0 is not proved to constrain the state constructed in Layer 1.
weaknesses: Once the six assumptions of this paper and the six imported lattice hypotheses are postulated, the main theorems (Proposition 3.8, Theorem 3.9, Theorem 4.11) reduce to immediate one-line consequences of the assumptions (telescoping of an assumed summable series and preserving a lower bound >= sigma_0 under an assumed limit).
The bridge in Appendix B only yields a non-summable O(g_k^2) bound (Eq. 35), leaving Assumption 3.5 unsubstantiated even conditionally on the companion lattice chain.

Layer 2 (Section 4) does not use any output of Layer 1 (Section 3); the existence of the dyadic continuum limit of Creutz ratios is simply assumed in Assumption 4.4 rather than derived from the RG-Cauchy framework.
Proposition 5.3 on SO(4) rotational invariance is purely heuristic and defers renormalized Schwinger functions, leaving the continuum state with only hypercubic symmetry.
